normalized_by_code: caveats[11]: note written from the KB (P-UAE-ISSUER)

reasoning: Step 1: Selected tariff line 32091010 (Acrylic emulsion paint) as the best match for 'acrylic paint' based on description; confidence high.
Step 2: The line has CEPA status PREFERENTIAL, so the preferential rate applies if origin qualifies.
Step 3: MFN rate is 10% (effective 10%), CEPA rate 0% per Table I S.No. 3502.
Step 4: Rule PSR-IN-R045 (CTSH + VA 40%) is met; all checks passed, so origin QUALIFIES.
Step 5: Duty saving estimated at 10000.00 AED (MFN 10% vs CEPA 0% on 100000 AED).
Step 6: Procedure steps cover factory registration, certificate application, fee payment, issuance, delivery, importer claim, and record keeping.
Step 7: Caveats include duty estimate on BCD only, other duties apply, '+' interpretation, and issuer ambiguity.

origin_result.basis: All checks passed: final manufacture in UAE, beyond minimal operations, tariff shift (all non-originating inputs outside subheading 320910), value addition 65% >= 40% on FOB basis.

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered before applying for a certificate of origin; registration takes about three working days and requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The application for a certificate of origin must include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service; the exporter logs in, fills in the form, uploads proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice, and submits.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000 (fee range AED 10 to AED 200), paid online.
The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers one import.
The goods must be shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage.
The exporter sends the certificate; if a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue, and must consent to verification visits.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
